1→# thos
     2→
     3→**the orchestrator you never knew you needed**
     4→
     5→A visual orchestration layer for [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code). Not another IDE — a UI that sits on top of the terminal-based agents you already use, solving the real friction of working with them day-to-day.
     6→
     7→## The Problem
     8→
     9→AI coding agents are powerful, but the experience of *using* them has real gaps:
    10→
    11→- **You lose track of what's happening.** Multiple agents running across tasks, and you're tab-switching and scrolling terminals to figure out who's doing what. The visibility problem compounds fast.
    12→
    13→- **Agents are smart but have the memory of an infant.** Your workflows are specific to you — your project structure, your preferences, your domain knowledge. The agent doesn't retain any of it between sessions. You end up re-explaining the same context over and over. A static CLAUDE.md helps, but it doesn't learn from your conversations or evolve with your codebase.
    14→
    15→- **Your machine is the bottleneck.** You have a laptop, not a build server. Agents want to compile, test, run — and your local machine can't keep up.
    16→
    17→- **Undoing things is painful.** Agent makes a wrong turn, and now you're doing forensics. Better change tracking, rollback, and context management should be table stakes — not an afterthought.
    18→
    19→- **Task management is manual.** Coordinating what gets done, in what order, across which agents — that's on you, in your head, with no tooling to help.
    20→
    21→## What thos Is
    22→
    23→thos is a UI wrapper around Claude Code. Terminals are fine — but when you're orchestrating work across agents, you need something more visual.
    24→
    25→Think of it as a control plane:
    26→
    27→- **Agent dashboard** — see what every agent is doing, in real time, at a glance
    28→- **Persistent memory** — agents that learn from your conversations and retain domain knowledge across sessions. Not just saved prompts — context that evolves with your codebase and workflows, so the first time you explain something is the last time.
    29→- **Change management** — track, diff, and roll back agent-generated changes with confidence
    30→- **Task orchestration** — assign, sequence, and track work across agents
    31→- **Remote access** — web UI accessible via localhost, with the option to expose over your network as needed
    32→
    33→## What thos Is Not
    34→
    35→- **Not an IDE.** VS Code, Cursor, Zed — these are well-engineered. thos doesn't compete with them; it complements them.
    36→- **Not a terminal replacement.** The terminal is the execution layer. thos is the visibility and coordination layer on top.
    37→- **Not a general agent framework.** Focused on Claude Code first. Breadth comes later, if it makes sense.
    38→
    39→## Prior Art
    40→

# Chat Condenser

## Context
When Claude does many consecutive tool calls (Grep, Glob, Read, Bash, etc.), the chat fills up with individual `[tool_use: Grep]` / `[tool_result: ...]` messages that push real conversation out of view. The condenser groups consecutive tool-only assistant messages into a single collapsible summary row.

## Approach

### 1. Enrich ChatMessage with tool metadata (`lib/types.ts`)
- Add `ToolCallInfo` interface (`name`, optional `toolUseId`)
- Add optional `toolCalls?: ToolCallInfo[]` and `isToolOnly?: boolean` to `ChatMessage`
- `isToolOnly` = true when the message has tool_use blocks but zero text blocks

### 2. Populate metadata at message creation (`hooks/use-websocket.ts`)
- In the `assistant` branch of `relayChatMessage()`, inspect content blocks to compute `toolCalls` and `isToolOnly`
- No changes to `extractText()` — display text stays the same

### 3. New grouping utility (`lib/condense-messages.ts`)
- Pure function `condenseMessages(messages: ChatMessage[]): DisplayItem[]`
- Linear pass: collects consecutive `isToolOnly` messages into `CondensedGroup` items
- Threshold: only condense when 2+ consecutive tool-only messages (single tool-only message renders normally)
- Non-tool messages, controlRequests, userQuestions, user messages, system messages all break the sequence
- Exports `SingleItem | CondensedGroup` union type (`DisplayItem`)
- `CondensedGroup` includes: summary string, tool counts breakdown, original messages array

### 4. New collapsible component (`components/dashboard/condensed-tool-group.tsx`)
- Collapsed: shows summary like "5 tool calls (Grep x3, Read x2)" with chevron icon
- Expanded: renders each original message using existing `<Message>` component, indented with a left border
- Uses `lucide-react` ChevronRight (already a dependency)

### 5. Integrate into chat rendering (`components/dashboard/chat.tsx`)
- `useMemo(() => condenseMessages(messages), [messages])` to get `displayItems`
- Replace `messages.map(...)` with `displayItems.map(...)` dispatching to `CondensedToolGroup` or existing components
- Raw view is unaffected (uses separate `rawMessages` array)

## Files
| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `lib/types.ts` | Edit — add `ToolCallInfo`, extend `ChatMessage` |
| `hooks/use-websocket.ts` | Edit — enrich assistant messages with `toolCalls`/`isToolOnly` |
| `lib/condense-messages.ts` | **New** — grouping utility |
| `components/dashboard/condensed-tool-group.tsx` | **New** — collapsible UI component |
| `components/dashboard/chat.tsx` | Edit — wire up condenser + new component |

## Verification
- Spawn a Claude agent and give it a task that triggers many tool calls (e.g. "search the codebase for all React hooks")
- Verify consecutive tool-only messages collapse into a single summary row
- Click to expand and confirm original messages render correctly
- Verify messages with actual text content from Claude are NOT condensed
- Verify control requests and user questions break the condensing sequence and render normally
- Verify raw view toggle still works and shows all messages uncondensed
